analysis:
Examined all eight batch analyses and all replayed patches/metadata; prior conclusions were not treated as proof. Replay is incomplete (40 of 54 source units omitted), notably the recovery implementation and bounded-shutdown helper, so material lifecycle questions remain unresolved.

Visible wiring queues memory/slot-limited startup candidates (ProviderLoop+StartupPreload.swift:307–310), records selected victims after successful Autopilot unload (Autopilot/ProviderLoop+Autopilot.swift:213), includes recovery in the busy gate (ProviderLoop+AutopilotBusy.swift:22), and cancels/waits for recovery during shutdown (ProviderLoop+Serve.swift:497). These changes affect A-018, TB-007 and TB-012/T-059. Documentation describes selection/pin protection, backoff, ordinary memory admission and hold cancellation; the replay does not independently verify their implementation. The internal testing seam exposes no demonstrated external invocation surface.

No supplied patch changes encryption, process-key custody, serving authorization, billing, cache scope, TTL or at-rest cryptography. Residency recovery alone does not establish a new T-041 disclosure. Added daemon diagnostics identify selections/recovery, not visibly prompts or credentials (ProviderLoop+Trust.swift:50–54). No concrete security regression is independently supported.

Further review must reconcile recovery's final load admission after suspension with hold/drain cancellation, selection changes, active-request protection and verified artifact bindings (T-012/T-027). Verify the ten-minute adopted-model release policy (changelog.d/selected-models-recover.md:8) actually drains requests and prevents immediate cold reload. Serve.swift:523 now delegates teardown; the reported 15-second bound must preserve native ownership until actual termination, including startup-cleanup callers, cache reclamation and logout (T-028/T-029, A-008/T-053). Missing replay of these implementations prevents resolving the local questions; it is not evidence of missing controls.
